item.title: Course teaches people to grow own food
item.description: Yamhill County Master Gardeners is seeking people who are low-income or live with food insecurity to participate in Garden to Table, a free, six-week course that teaches how to grow produce in raised beds. The program will start Feb. 14 and continue each Saturdays through March 21. English-language sessions will be from 10 a.m. to noon at three sites: the Extension auditorium on Lafayette Avenue in McMinnville, the Bridge Learning Community in Sheridan and St. Michael’s Episcopal Church, Newberg

item.title: Narthex Gallery features local views
item.description: Paintings by Christa Brandenburg of McMinnville will be featured through March 30 in the First Presbyterian Church’s Narthex Gallery, 390 N.E. Second St. The show is called “That Spark of Being.” It features landscape views the artist saw within 1,000 feet of her studio in downtown McMinnville, such as the warehouse buildings in the Granary District. item.description: Sociologists call “groupthink” the tendency of cohesive social groups to never question group decisions. item.title: Jeb Bladine: Challenges in a new chapter of city government
item.description: McMinnville, now embarked on a new chapter in city government, has challenges galore in areas of finance, operations, special projects and community trust. It begins with planning for a new budget year, which already has been promised to continue tax-and-spend programs that propagated so much public controversy. item.title: Those who covet power must first earn out trust
item.description: For the first 150 years of its statehood, Oregon limited regular legislative sessions to odd-numbered years. As governance turned increasingly complex and contentious, it became one of only a handful of states still getting by without annual sessions. item.title: Jonah Goldberg: Trump’s brand of globalism stands to impoverish us all
item.description: About the writer: Conservative D.C.-based commentator Jonah Goldberg serves as editor-in-chief of The Dispatch, hosts The Remnant podcast, authors a weekly Los Angeles Times column, holds a chair with the American Enterprise Institute and serves as a commentator with NPR and CNN. Previously, he spent 21 years as an editor at The National Review and 10 as a commentator at Fox News. He’s the author of three New York Times best sellers. I’m not sure what to call the new era we seem to be entering.

item.title: Eric Schuck: Don’t let discordant notes mar symphony of the Fed
item.description: About the writer: Eric Schuck holds a Ph.D. in economics from Washington State University and a professorship in economics at Linfield University. He’s twice been honored with Fulbright Fellowships to work and study abroad, once in South Africa and once in Lebanon. An officer in the Navy Reserve, he’s also served a pair of active-duty military tours in the Middle East.
